author: fwyzard
body: #### PR description: Replace the one-byte-at-a-time implementation `cms::Adler32` with a call to the zlib implementation. The old implementation runs at ~0.46 GB/s and takes ~55% of the time of the streamer input source on raw data events; zlib's version gives identical checksums at ~3.6 GB/s. Here's a comparison on raw data and HLT scouting events, with 1, 8, and 31 threads and streams per job, on an AMD EPYC 9534. The jobs are pinned to the corresponding number of physical cores, without SMT siblings. The results show the average and standard deviation of 4 repetitions. | file | threads | cms::Adler32 | zlib `adler32_z` | ISA-L `isal_adler32`| |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | raw data, 10k events | 1 | 236.0 0.3 | 445.4 1.3 (1.89) | 495.8 0.7 (2.10) | | raw data, 10k events | 8 | 229.2 0.3 | 433.1 1.9 (1.89) | 477.6 1.6 (2.08) | | raw data, 10k events | 31 | 213.8 0.3 | 388.7 1.9 (1.82) | 426.0 0.2 (1.99) | | HLT scouting, 13k events | 1 | 3162 29 | 3854 35 (1.22) | 3919 24 (1.24) | | HLT scouting, 13k events | 8 | 2859 19 | 3352 50 (1.17) | 3508 22 (1.23) | | HLT scouting, 13k events | 31 | 2397 14 | 2972 15 (1.24) | 2995 30 (1.25) | As the table and plot show, we could get another 0-10% speedup using the Intel ISA-L implementation, if it's OK to add it as a new dependency. Rename `cms::Adler32` to `cms::adler32` following the CMS coding rules, and simplify the API to use a single `uint32_t` argument and return value. Update all client code, and remove the checksum state of `FRDOutputModule` and `RawEventFileWriterForBU`, which was reset but never updated or read, the unused `StreamerFileWriter::get_adler32()`, and the unused includes of `Adler32Calculator.h`. #### PR validation: The zlib implementation gives identical result to the old CMS implementation. All unit tests pass.
title: Improve adler32 api and use zlib implementation
